title: Sheaf cohomology and higher direct images
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. The cohomology functors $\mathrm H^p(X,-)$ are
the right derived functors of the global sections functor $\Gamma(X,-)$
on $\mathcal O_X$-modules; a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules gives a long exact cohomology sequence. For a morphism
$f:X\to S$, the higher direct images $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ are the right
derived functors of $f_*$.
(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.11, Tag
[01EO](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01EO), and Section
20.13, Tag
[01EY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01EY).*)

proof.text: For an $\mathcal O_X$-module, use the established ringed-space module-cohomology definition: choose an injective resolution and take the cohomology of its global-sections complex; this is independent of the resolution and realizes the right derived functors of global sections. This is exactly the cohomology functor $\mathrm H^p(X,-)$ in the item.

For a morphism of schemes, regard it as a morphism of ringed spaces. The direct image on module sheaves is an additive pushforward functor, and its derived direct image is defined by applying pushforward to a K-injective resolution, with $Rf_*\mathcal F$ represented by $f_*\mathcal J$ for every K-injective resolution $\mathcal F[0]\to\mathcal J$. An injective resolution $\mathcal F[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ (which exists as $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives) is a bounded below complex of injectives, hence K-injective; so $H^p(Rf_*\mathcal F)=H^p(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$, which is the $p$-th right derived functor $R^p f_*\mathcal F$ computed by injective resolutions. This is the higher-direct-image clause.

The category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian with enough injectives, and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and left exact. Right derived functors of a left exact additive functor on such a category form a universal delta-functor. Applying this to global sections, whose right derived functors are $\mathrm H^p(X,-)$ by the first step, gives connecting morphisms for every short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and the associated long exact cohomology sequence.
